title: Federal awards that name San Francisco work
question: Which of those federal awards describe work in San Francisco itself, where the City may be paying for the same programme?
finding: 9 federal awards to 5 of these organisations name San Francisco in their description, $7.8 million in all. Public Health Institute: $2.1 million from the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (2017); Public Health Institute: $1.5 million from the National Institutes of Health (2017); Public Health Institute: $994,407 from the Environmental Protection Agency (2021); Main Street Launch: $800,000 from the Administration for Children and Families (2024). These are the awards where a federal and a City grant could pay for the same San Francisco programme; the grant budgets would show whether costs are split.
how: The kept award rows of the previous screen whose description contains the words San Francisco.
limits: Co-funding one programme from several sources is the ordinary way nonprofits are financed and is often required as a match; it becomes a problem only if the same expense is claimed twice. Descriptions are short and many awards working in the city will not name it.
